_comment: S3 lifecycle policy — shramsafal-uploads-prod.
spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
Owner: infra-cofounder (author-only) + founder (apply). AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED.
THIS IS THE ONE DESIRED-STATE TRANSACTION FOR THIS BUCKET — do not apply the
bullets under §11 piecemeal; put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration replaces the
WHOLE document, so a second partial apply silently reverts this one.
LIVE POLICY CAPTURED VERBATIM 2026-08-15 (READ-ONLY, aws s3api
get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket shramsafal-uploads-prod) — THIS IS
THE ROLLBACK. To roll back this whole change, re-apply exactly this document:
"Rules": [
"ID": "shramsafal-retention",
"Filter": {"Prefix": ""},
"Status": "Enabled",
"Transitions": [{"Days": 365, "StorageClass": "GLACIER"}],
"Expiration": {"Days": 2555}
(also saved verbatim by apply-config.sh into the capture/ subfolder it creates
at run time, timestamped, so the rollback record is never only in this file).
WHAT CHANGED AND WHY (three inputs, landed as ONE document):
1. Glacier transition REMOVED, no replacement. Flexible Retrieval cannot be
read without a 3-5h restore or an expedited-retrieval fee; one 'show me
last season' tap would cost 13x-164x that photo's whole annual storage
bill. Nothing has transitioned yet (34/34 objects still Standard as of
the plan's own measurement; first transition would have fired
2027-05-03) — this is a pure config replace, no restore/copy/cost.
Do NOT substitute Standard-IA (128 KB minimum billable size makes
thumbnails MORE expensive) or GLACIER_IR (deferred until attachments/
exceeds 100 GB — not close today).
2. The single bucket-wide rule is SPLIT BY PREFIX. The live rule carried
the farmer-evidence 7-year expiry AND the Glacier transition on the
SAME rule at prefix "" (bucket-wide) — so 'remove Glacier' is not a
separate edit, it means rewriting the rule that also carries the
farmer-evidence retention. Below, retention lives on attachments/
ONLY; the four other prefixes get their own scoped rules.
3. Deploy-ish prefixes get a MEASURED expiry, not a round number. The
bucket holds 618 MB across FOUR non-evidence, non-APK prefixes —
_deploy/, _deploys/, deploys/, ai-sessions/ — none of which were named
in the original 'give the deploy prefix a 180-day expiry' draft (there
is no single 'the deploy prefix'; there are four, and 180 is a round
number, not a measurement). Manual RDS snapshots never expire, and
§15 promises 'redeploy the previous SHA' with no horizon — so an
artifact expiry shorter than the oldest retained manual snapshot's age
would manufacture a database rollback point with no matching binary.
DEPLOY_PREFIX_EXPIRY_DAYS below is a PLACEHOLDER computed once at
capture time (see next block) — apply-config.sh RECOMPUTES it fresh on
every run via compute-deploy-horizon.sh and overwrites this field
before the API call. Manual snapshots never age out on their own, so
this number MUST be recomputed at every apply, not read verbatim from
this file — a stale copy of this file understates the required
horizon more with every day that passes.
DEPLOY_PREFIX_EXPIRY_DAYS PROVENANCE (measured 2026-08-15 via
aws/uploads/compute-deploy-horizon.sh, read-only):
aws rds describe-db-snapshots --region ap-south-1 --snapshot-type manual
Oldest retained: shramsafal-prod-db-g2-8eec0e72-20260609t115008z, created
+ 30-day safety buffer (stated constant, applied to the measured base —
not a substitute for it) = 96 days.
Placeholder value in this file: 96. compute-deploy-horizon.sh recomputes
this on every apply/audit run; treat the number in this file as a dated
worked example, not the live truth.
apk/ GETS NO RULE AT ALL (by deliberate omission) — expiring it breaks live
APK download links. It still benefits from the bucket-wide
AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload rule below, which never touches complete
objects.
attachments/ keeps its 7-year Expiration (farmer evidence, unchanged in
substance) but LOSES the Glacier transition (item 1 above).
The four deploy-ish prefixes ALSO get NoncurrentVersionExpiration at the
same horizon — this bucket has versioning ON (confirmed live), so a
current-version Expiration alone only inserts a delete marker and moves the
bytes to noncurrent; without a paired noncurrent rule the 618 MB never
actually leaves the bucket. This pairing is SAFE here because these four
prefixes hold nothing but reproducible build/session artifacts — this is
exactly the class of prefix the raw-bucket incident report says a
noncurrent rule may safely target. It is NOT applied to attachments/ or
apk/, and it is NOT applied anywhere on the raw bucket (see aws/raw/).
D9 CHECK (voice retention is FOREVER, per founder ruling D9): this bucket
does not hold raw voice audio — that lives in agrisync-raw-ap-south-1
(see aws/raw/lifecycle-policy.json, which authors NO expiration of any
kind). attachments/ here holds photos/receipts, not voice; its retention
is unchanged (still 2555 days) by this transaction. No rule in this
document shortens, transitions, or expires anything D9 covers.
AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload is bucket-wide and safe on every prefix —
it only cleans up multipart uploads that never completed; it cannot
delete or move a completed object.
APPLY (founder only, via apply-config.sh — do NOT call put-bucket-lifecycle-
configuration directly, or the DEPLOY_PREFIX_EXPIRY_DAYS placeholder above
will be applied verbatim instead of the recomputed value):
bash aws/uploads/apply-config.sh --apply
VERIFY:
aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket shramsafal-uploads-prod --region ap-south-1
